Deployers must design and maintain a risk management policy for the AI systems they use.
Deployers must complete an impact assessment before deploying high-risk AI systems.
Consumers must be notified when a high-risk AI system is used to make consequential decisions about them.

summary: Prohibiting a person from utilizing certain personal identifying information or engaging in certain conduct in order to cause certain harm; prohibiting a person from using certain artificial intelligence or certain deepfake representations for certai...
title: Criminal Law – Identity Fraud – Artificial Intelligence and Deepfake Representations
scope: This bill applies to individuals and entities that utilize personal identifying information or engage in conduct that causes harm, including those using artificial intelligence or deepfake representations. It specifically targets individuals who may use such technologies maliciously or fraudulently. The scope includes any person who may engage in identity fraud or related activities.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems as defined in the State Finance and Procurement Article, which includes machine-based systems that can make predictions, recommendations, or decisions. It also addresses deepfake representations, which are defined as images or recordings indistinguishable from actual human beings. These technologies are regulated when used to impersonate or mislead individuals.
keyRequirements: Prohibits the use of personal identifying information without consent to cause harm.
Prohibits the use of artificial intelligence or deepfake representations to impersonate or mislead individuals.
Allows victims to bring civil action against those who commit violations.
Establishes penalties for violations based on the value of benefits obtained through fraudulent means.

summary: Requiring a developer of a generative artificial intelligence system, on or before January 1, 2026, and before the developer releases or substantially modifies a certain generative artificial intelligence system, to publish on the developer's website...
title: Generative Artificial Intelligence – Training Data Transparency
scope: This bill applies to developers of generative artificial intelligence systems, which can include private companies and state or local government entities that design, code, produce, or substantially modify such systems. It is relevant to any entity that releases or modifies generative AI systems for public use in Maryland.
modelsCovered: The bill specifically covers generative artificial intelligence systems, which are defined as AI that can generate derived synthetic content such as text, images, video, and audio. It includes systems that are released for use by the general public and those that are considered high-risk AI systems impacting individuals or communities.
keyRequirements: Developers must publish documentation detailing the data used to train their generative AI systems on their website before release or substantial modification.
Documentation must include sources or owners of the data, a description of how the data furthers the intended purpose, and the number of data points in the dataset.
Developers must disclose whether any data are in the public domain or protected by copyright, trademark, or patent.
Developers must indicate whether the data include personal information or aggregate consumer information.
Developers must provide information on the time period during which the data were collected and whether the data collection is ongoing.
sponsor: Delegates Wu, Qi, Bagnall, Hill, Mireku –North, Phillips, Ruth, Schindler, and Ziegler

summary: Establishing that a person who intentionally, knowingly, or negligently designs or creates artificial intelligence software able to cause physical injury or death is strictly liable for damages and subject to a civil penalty if the software is used t...
title: Artificial Intelligence – Causing Injury or Death – Civil and Criminal Liability
scope: The bill applies to individuals or entities that design or create artificial intelligence software capable of causing physical injury or death. This includes any person or organization involved in the development of such software, regardless of size or industry sector.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence software that is capable of causing personal injury or death. This includes any AI systems that may be designed with the potential to inflict harm on individuals, without specifying particular types or categories of AI technologies.
keyRequirements: Individuals must be strictly liable for damages resulting from personal injury or death caused by their AI software.
Individuals are prohibited from intentionally designing or creating AI software that can cause injury or death.
Individuals are prohibited from knowingly designing or creating AI software that can cause injury or death.
Individuals are prohibited from negligently designing or creating AI software that can cause injury or death.
Violations of the prohibitions may result in civil penalties or criminal charges, including felonies and misdemeanors.

summary: Relative to issuing guidance regarding setting policies for the use of AI in schools. Education.
title: An Act relative to issuing guidance regarding setting policies for the use of AI in schools.
scope: This bill applies to school districts and charter schools in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. It is intended for educators and administrators responsible for setting policies regarding the use of artificial intelligence in educational settings.
modelsCovered: The bill covers the use of artificial intelligence (AI) programs by students and educators in the classroom. It addresses the benefits and limitations of AI in education, including considerations for safe usage and equity implications.
keyRequirements: The commissioner shall issue guidelines for the usage of AI programs by students and educators.
Guidance must include the benefits and limitations of AI in education.
The department shall hold a minimum of three public hearings to gather input from stakeholders.
The commissioner shall update the guidelines as necessary and publish them annually on the department’s website by September 1.

summary: For legislation to establish a commission to investigate AI in education. Education.
title: An Act to establish a commission to investigate AI in education.
scope: This bill applies to the independent school systems of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, including both private and public entities. It involves various stakeholders such as local school committees, superintendents, and local town governments.
modelsCovered: The bill covers generative AI systems, including AI chatbots like ChatGPT, and automated decision systems used by school systems. These technologies are utilized for tasks such as scheduling, lesson planning, grading, and other educational purposes.
keyRequirements: Conduct a complete survey of all uses of automated decision systems and generative AI in school systems.
Provide guidelines for the ethical use of AI in teaching and learning.
Make recommendations for protecting data of schools that use AI.
Evaluate the implementation and use of automated decision systems and generative AI in education.
Consult with experts in machine learning, algorithmic bias, and civil rights.
Examine research related to disparate outcomes from automated decision systems.
Assess data protection laws and compliance related to automated decision systems.

summary: Relative to artificial intelligence health communications and informed patient consent. Financial Services.
title: An Act relative to AI health communications and informed patient consent
scope: This bill applies to healthcare providers and insurance carriers operating within the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. It mandates compliance with regulations regarding patient consent and the use of artificial intelligence in health communications. The bill is relevant to entities involved in the healthcare sector, particularly those utilizing AI in their operations.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems used in healthcare communications and decision-making processes. This includes automated decision tools and algorithms utilized in claims review and utilization review processes. The focus is on ensuring transparency and minimizing bias in AI systems affecting patient care.
keyRequirements: Patients must be informed if information they receive has been generated by artificial intelligence.
Healthcare providers must provide instructions on how to contact a human provider if AI-generated information was not reviewed by a provider.
Insurance carriers must disclose the use of AI algorithms in the claims review process, including a summary of the tools used.
Carriers must submit an annual report detailing AI algorithms and data training sets used in utilization review, ensuring they minimize bias based on various demographic factors.

summary: For legislation relative to the use of artificial intelligence and other software tools in healthcare decision-making. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act relative to the use of artificial intelligence and other software tools in healthcare decision-making
scope: This bill applies to carriers and utilization review organizations that utilize artificial intelligence or other software tools for utilization review or management functions in healthcare. It specifically targets entities involved in healthcare decision-making processes, ensuring compliance with regulations regarding the use of such technologies.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems, algorithms, and software tools used for utilization review or management functions in healthcare. It defines artificial intelligence as an engineered or machine-based system that can infer outputs based on inputs, influencing healthcare decisions.
keyRequirements: The AI system must base its determinations on an insured's medical history and individual clinical circumstances.
The AI system must not base its determinations solely on a group dataset.
The AI system's criteria and guidelines must comply with applicable state and federal law.
The AI system must not supplant healthcare provider decision-making.
The AI system must not discriminate against any insured in violation of state or federal law.
The AI system must be open to inspection for audit or compliance reviews.
Disclosures regarding the use of the AI system must be included in written policies and procedures.
The AI system's performance and outcomes must be periodically reviewed to maximize accuracy and reliability.
Patient data must not be used beyond its intended purpose and must comply with state and federal law.
The AI system must not cause harm to the insured.

summary: For legislation to promote economic development with emerging artificial intelligence models and safety. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act promoting economic development with emerging artificial intelligence models and safety.
scope: This bill applies to private companies developing or deploying artificial intelligence models in key industry sectors, as well as entities operating computing clusters that provide resources for training such models. It targets organizations involved in the development of artificial intelligence and those that may be impacted by its deployment, including technology companies and research institutions.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence models that are classified as 'covered models', which are defined based on their training requirements and computational costs. These include models that require significant computing power and financial investment, specifically those that could potentially cause or materially enable critical harm.
keyRequirements: Establish a safety and security protocol for the development and operation of covered models.
Conduct annual reviews of safety and security protocols and retain records for a minimum of five years.
Report any artificial intelligence safety incidents to the attorney general within 72 hours.
Implement reasonable cybersecurity protections to prevent unauthorized access to covered models.
Obtain and retain customer identifying information when utilizing computing resources for training covered models.

summary: For legislation relative to AI-generated child sexual abuse material. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act relative to AI-generated child sexual abuse material
scope: This bill applies to entities involved in the creation, distribution, or possession of visual material depicting minors, including government agencies and private organizations that handle such materials. It specifically addresses those who may produce or disseminate AI-generated content that could be construed as child sexual abuse material.
modelsCovered: The bill covers AI systems that generate visual material, particularly those that utilize digitization to create images that may appear to depict minors. This includes technologies that produce computer-generated images that could mislead a reasonable person into believing they depict a minor.
keyRequirements: Amend Section 29C of chapter 272 of the General Laws to include visual material produced by digitization.
Define 'Digitization' as the creation or alteration of visual material that appears to depict a minor.
Include visual material produced by digitization in the definition of 'visual material'.

summary: For legislation relative to AI-generated child sexual abuse material, report the accompanying bill (Senate, No. 2633).
title: An Act relative to AI-generated child sexual abuse material
scope: This bill applies to individuals who create child sexual abuse visual material with knowledge that the person is a minor or with reason to know that the person is a minor. It also pertains to any entities involved in the production, processing, or dissemination of such material.
modelsCovered: The bill addresses AI-generated child sexual abuse visual material, which includes any visual material depicting sexual conduct or a minor in a state of nudity that has been created or altered using AI technologies. It specifically mentions the creation of visual material that falsely represents a minor.
keyRequirements: Whoever creates child sexual abuse visual material with knowledge that the person is a minor shall be punished by imprisonment or fines.
The determination of whether the child in the visual material is a minor can be made through various forms of testimony.
Amendments to existing laws to include provisions related to child sexual abuse visual material.

summary: For legislation relative to the use of artificial intelligence and other software tools in healthcare decision-making, report the accompanying bill (Senate, No. 2632).
title: An Act relative to the use of artificial intelligence and other software tools in healthcare decision-making.
scope: This bill applies to licensed professionals providing therapy or psychotherapy services in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. It also pertains to corporations or entities that provide, advertise, or offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including those utilizing artificial intelligence tools. Additionally, it affects carriers or utilization review organizations involved in healthcare decision-making processes.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems that assist licensed professionals in providing administrative and supplementary support in therapy or psychotherapy services. It includes engineered or machine-based systems that can infer from input to generate outputs influencing healthcare environments. The bill specifically addresses the use of artificial intelligence in utilization review and management functions related to medical necessity.
keyRequirements: Licensed professionals must maintain full responsibility for all interactions and data use associated with AI systems.
Patients must be informed in writing about the use of AI and its specific purpose, and consent must be obtained.
AI cannot make independent therapeutic decisions or directly interact with clients in therapeutic communication.
All records and communications must remain confidential and not be disclosed except as required by law.
Violators may face civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, assessed by the division after a hearing.

summary: For legislation to promote economic development with emerging artificial intelligence models and safety, report the accompanying bill (Senate, No. 2630).
title: An Act promoting economic development with emerging artificial intelligence models and safety.
scope: This bill applies to large frontier developers, defined as those with annual gross revenues exceeding $500 million. It also includes private companies developing or deploying artificial intelligence models in key industry sectors as enumerated in the bill. The bill is relevant to entities involved in the development and deployment of frontier AI technologies.
modelsCovered: The bill covers frontier models, which are defined as foundation models trained using a significant amount of computing power. These models are characterized by their ability to influence physical or virtual environments and may pose catastrophic risks if mismanaged. The legislation also addresses the management of catastrophic risks associated with the deployment of these models.
keyRequirements: Large frontier developers must write, implement, and publish a frontier AI framework that addresses catastrophic risks.
Developers are required to conduct assessments of catastrophic risks for their frontier models and publish transparency reports before deploying new or modified models.
The Attorney General must be notified of any critical safety incidents within specified timeframes.
Developers must provide a mechanism for covered employees to report safety concerns without retaliation.

summary: For legislation to protect consumers interacting with artificial intelligence chatbots. Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure.
title: An Act establishing protections for consumers interacting with artificial intelligence chatbots
scope: This bill applies to commercial entities that deploy chatbots for interaction with consumers. It is relevant to businesses of all sizes that utilize automated programs for customer engagement, regardless of their revenue or employee count. The geographic scope is limited to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
modelsCovered: The bill covers chatbots, defined as automated programs designed to simulate conversation with human users. This includes technologies that use generative artificial intelligence or similar methods, employing audio, visual, or textual communication.
keyRequirements: Commercial entities must clearly and conspicuously disclose to users that they are interacting with a chatbot and not a human.
Interactions with chatbots shall have the same legal force and effect as interactions with a human agent of the commercial entity.
Use of a disclaimer shall not constitute a defense under this chapter or any other related laws.

summary: Relative to reducing emissions from artificial intelligence. Economic Development and Emerging Technologies.
title: An Act reducing emissions from artificial intelligence
scope: This bill applies to covered entities, which include any entity or person, excluding individuals acting in a non-commercial context, that operates a search engine with an artificial intelligence or generative artificial intelligence service. It does not include government agencies or entities with average annual gross revenues not exceeding $10,000,000 in the past three calendar years.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence technologies, including but not limited to machine learning, generative artificial intelligence used to produce or edit text, audio, images, or video media, and any data systems or applications that operate using artificial intelligence. It specifically addresses the environmental impacts associated with the lifecycle of these AI models and systems.
keyRequirements: Covered entities must obtain affirmative consent from users before utilizing artificial intelligence in search results.
The Executive Office of Technology Services and Security must recognize acceptable mechanisms for individuals to exercise affirmative consent.
A comprehensive study on the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence must be conducted and reported within 18 months of enactment.
Reporting entities must monitor and report their annual environmental impacts, including carbon emissions and water usage, to the Department of Energy and Environmental Affairs.
Entities failing to report their annual environmental impacts may face penalties up to $20,000.

summary: Relative to provenance regarding artificial intelligence. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act regulating provenance regarding artificial intelligence
scope: This bill applies to GenAI Providers, which are organizations that develop GenAI Tools made publicly available for use by Massachusetts residents. It also applies to Large Online Platforms that distribute content to users who did not create or collaborate in creating the content.
modelsCovered: The bill covers generative AI systems, specifically those that produce or modify visual and/or audio content, referred to as Synthetic Content. It also includes definitions for GenAI Models, which are designed to generate new data or content based on training data patterns.
keyRequirements: A GenAI Provider must apply Provenance Data to wholly-generated Synthetic Content.
A GenAI Provider must make available a Provenance Application Tool for users to apply Provenance Data to modified Content.
A GenAI Provider must provide a Provenance Reader to the public.
A Large Online Platform must retain available Provenance Data in Content provided to it.
A Large Online Platform must make Provenance Data available to consumers of Content or indicate its availability.
A Capture Device must include the ability to enable Provenance Data inclusion in captured Content.

summary: For legislation to regulate the use of artificial intelligence. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act fostering artificial intelligence responsibility
scope: This bill applies to employers operating within the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, including private companies, government entities, and public authorities. It specifically targets organizations that utilize automated decision systems in their employment practices, regardless of size or industry sector. The legislation mandates compliance for all entities that engage in electronic monitoring and automated decision-making related to employment.
modelsCovered: The bill covers automated decision systems (ADS) that utilize machine learning, statistical modeling, and data analytics to assist or replace human decision-making in employment-related decisions. It includes systems that generate outputs impacting candidates or employees, such as scoring, classification, and recommendations. Additionally, the legislation addresses electronic monitoring tools that collect employee data.
keyRequirements: Employers must provide prior written notice and obtain consent from employees before using electronic monitoring tools.
Automated employment decision tools must undergo an impact assessment conducted by an independent auditor.
Employers are required to establish meaningful human oversight for decisions based on data collected through electronic monitoring.
Employers must ensure that any employee data collected is stored securely and disposed of when no longer needed.
Employers cannot use electronic monitoring tools in a manner that violates labor or civil rights laws.

summary: For legislation to ensure accountability and transparency in artificial intelligence systems. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act to ensure accountability and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
scope: This bill applies to developers and deployers of artificial intelligence systems in Massachusetts, including individuals and entities that create or utilize AI technologies. It specifically addresses responsibilities for corporations and organizations that use AI systems to influence consumer decisions, particularly those that are considered high-risk. Small businesses with fewer than 50 employees are exempt from certain provisions.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems that process inputs to generate outputs influencing decisions in various sectors, including education, employment, finance, housing, healthcare, insurance, and legal services. It defines high-risk AI systems as those that materially influence consequential decisions, and includes provisions for algorithmic discrimination and transparency in AI usage.
keyRequirements: Developers must identify, mitigate, and disclose risks of algorithmic discrimination.
Developers must provide deployers with documentation including intended uses and known limitations of AI systems.
Deployers of high-risk AI systems must implement a risk management program aligned with industry standards.
Deployers must complete annual impact assessments for each high-risk AI system.
Corporations must disclose the purpose and methods of AI use to target specific consumer groups.

summary: Relative to consumers interactions with artificial intelligence systems. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act protecting consumers in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
scope: This bill applies to developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems operating within the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. It includes private companies and organizations that develop or deploy AI technologies that impact consumers. The bill does not specify size thresholds for compliance, but it mandates that all entities engaging with high-risk AI systems adhere to the outlined requirements.
modelsCovered: The bill covers high-risk artificial intelligence systems that are defined as those making consequential decisions affecting consumers. This includes systems that influence decisions related to education, employment, financial services, healthcare, housing, and insurance. The legislation specifically addresses algorithmic discrimination and the responsibilities of developers and deployers in mitigating such risks.
keyRequirements: Developers must use reasonable care to protect consumers from known risks of algorithmic discrimination.
Developers must provide documentation detailing the intended uses and known limitations of high-risk AI systems.
Deployers must implement a risk management policy to govern the deployment of high-risk AI systems.
Deployers must complete an impact assessment for high-risk AI systems within six months of deployment.
Consumers must be notified when a high-risk AI system is used to make consequential decisions affecting them.
sponsor: David M. Rogers and Andres X. Vargas

summary: Relative to artificial intelligence disclosures. Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity.
title: An Act relative to artificial intelligence disclosure
scope: This bill applies to any person located within the Commonwealth of Massachusetts using a generative artificial intelligence system to create or repurpose audio, video, text, or print AI-generated content. It encompasses all individuals and entities engaged in the creation of such content, regardless of their size or industry sector.
modelsCovered: The bill covers generative artificial intelligence systems that create or modify content such as audio, video, print, or text. It specifically addresses AI-generated content, which is defined as content substantially created or modified by these systems, impacting the meaning or significance of the original content.
keyRequirements: Generative artificial intelligence systems must include a clear and conspicuous disclosure identifying the content as AI-generated.
The disclosure must be permanent or uneasily removed by subsequent users.
Metadata must include identification of the content as AI-generated, the identity of the system used, and the date and time of creation.
Users of generative AI systems are prohibited from removing any notice or disclosure related to AI-generated content.

summary: By Representative Jones of North Reading, a petition of Bradley H. Jones, Jr., and others for an investigation and study by a special legislative commission (including members of the General Court) to study load growth due to AI and data centers. Adv...
title: An Act establishing a special legislative commission to study load growth due to AI and data centers.
scope: The bill applies to a special legislative commission established to study load growth due to AI and data centers. This includes members of the General Court, specifically legislators and appointed officials from various governmental departments. The focus is on understanding the implications of load growth on state resources and infrastructure.
modelsCovered: The bill addresses load growth driven by data centers that support high-performance computing and artificial intelligence. It encompasses the impact of industrial growth and electrification on electricity demand, particularly in relation to AI technologies used in these contexts.
keyRequirements: Establishment of a special legislative commission to study load growth due to AI and data centers.
The commission's study must include surges in electricity demand driven by data centers.
The commission shall submit its report and recommendations to the clerk’s office of the house of representatives and the senate within one year after the passage of this act.

summary: Insurance: health insurers; use of artificial intelligence tools to make decisions regarding claims; prohibit. Amends 1956 PA 218 (MCL 500.100 - 500.8302) by adding sec. 3406ss.
title: Insurance: health insurers; use of artificial intelligence tools to make decisions regarding claims; prohibit.

The legislation does not specify particular types of AI technologies but emphasizes the prohibition of AI in claims decision processes.
keyRequirements: Prohibit health insurers from using artificial intelligence tools to make decisions regarding claims.
Amend existing legislation related to health insurance practices.
Ensure compliance with the new provisions outlined in the bill.

summary: Human services: medical services; use of artificial intelligence tools to make decisions regarding claims; prohibit. Amends 1939 PA 280 (MCL 400.1 - 400.119b) by adding sec. 107b.

scope: This bill applies to healthcare providers and organizations involved in the processing of medical claims. The legislation aims to regulate the deployment of these AI technologies in sensitive areas such as medical services.
keyRequirements: Prohibit the use of artificial intelligence tools for making decisions regarding medical claims.
Amend existing laws to include provisions against AI decision-making in healthcare claims.
Ensure compliance with the new regulations by healthcare providers.

summary: Trade: business regulation; requirements and safety standards for developers of certain artificial intelligence models; provide for. Creates new act.

scope: This bill applies to developers of artificial intelligence models, specifically targeting private companies engaged in the development and deployment of AI technologies. It encompasses organizations that may have significant influence or control over AI systems, including those operating in various industry sectors such as technology, finance, and healthcare. The bill aims to establish a regulatory framework for these entities to ensure compliance with safety and operational standards.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence models that are classified as high-risk, particularly those that may impact critical infrastructure or public safety. It includes generative AI systems and automated decision-making technologies that are utilized in sectors such as healthcare, hiring, and public service. The focus is on ensuring that these AI systems meet specific safety and ethical standards.
keyRequirements: Developers must adhere to safety standards for AI model deployment.
Regular audits and assessments of AI systems are required to ensure compliance.
Transparency in AI decision-making processes must be maintained.
Developers must implement measures to mitigate risks associated with AI technologies.

summary: Crimes: other; use of artificial intelligence to commit certain crimes; prohibit. Amends 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.1 - 750.568) by adding sec. 411y.
title: Prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to commit certain crimes
scope: This bill applies to individuals and entities that may utilize artificial intelligence in the commission of crimes. It targets all persons and organizations that might employ AI technologies in unlawful activities, without specific size thresholds or industry limitations mentioned.
modelsCovered: The bill addresses the use of artificial intelligence systems in the context of committing crimes. It does not specify particular types of AI systems but emphasizes the prohibition of using AI to facilitate illegal activities, which could encompass various AI technologies.
keyRequirements: Prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to commit crimes
Amend existing laws to include provisions related to AI
Establish penalties for violations of the prohibition

summary: Prohibition from using artificial intelligence to dynamically set product prices
title: Prohibition from using artificial intelligence to dynamically set product prices
scope: This bill applies to individuals and entities that engage in the pricing of products, specifically prohibiting them from utilizing artificial intelligence for dynamic pricing adjustments. It targets private companies involved in retail or e-commerce that may adjust prices based on various market factors.
modelsCovered: The bill covers machine-based systems classified as artificial intelligence that infer outputs from inputs to influence pricing decisions. This includes systems that adjust, fix, or control product prices in real time based on market demands, competitor prices, and customer behavior.
keyRequirements: Prohibition on using artificial intelligence to adjust product prices in real time.
Compliance with enforcement actions by the attorney general under section 8.31.

summary: Algorithm and AI use prohibited during health insurance prior authorization request review.
title: A bill for an act relating to health insurance; prohibiting algorithm or artificial intelligence use during prior authorization request review
scope: This bill applies to health carriers, which include insurance companies and other entities that provide health insurance coverage. It is relevant to all health plans offered, sold, issued, or renewed in the state of Minnesota.
modelsCovered: The bill covers the use of algorithms and artificial intelligence programs specifically in the context of making determinations for prior authorization requests in health insurance. It prohibits the use of these technologies when approving or denying such requests.
keyRequirements: Health carriers are prohibited from using algorithms or artificial intelligence programs for prior authorization request determinations.
The prohibition applies to all health plans offered, sold, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.

summary: Study of environmental impacts of artificial intelligence required, report required, and money appropriated.
title: Study of environmental impacts of artificial intelligence required, report required, and money appropriated.
scope: This bill applies to the Pollution Control Agency of Minnesota, which is responsible for conducting the study and preparing the report on environmental impacts. It involves engagement with stakeholders, including those with expertise relevant to the study and interested members of the general public.

keyRequirements: Submit a report on the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence by January 1, 2027.
Include assessments of energy consumption and pollution associated with AI models and hardware.
Identify potential acute environmental impacts at local scales.
Engage with stakeholders and the general public during the study.

summary: Artificial intelligence use to dynamically set product prices prohibited.
title: A bill for an act relating to consumer protection; prohibiting a person from using artificial intelligence to dynamically set product prices
scope: This bill applies to any person or entity that engages in the practice of setting product prices. It includes private companies and businesses that utilize pricing strategies based on market conditions, competitor pricing, and customer behavior. The law is intended to protect consumers from dynamic pricing practices influenced by artificial intelligence.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems that are capable of dynamically adjusting product prices in real time. This includes machine-based systems that infer outputs based on various inputs such as market demands and competitor prices. The focus is on AI technologies that influence pricing decisions rather than on specific types of AI models.
keyRequirements: Prohibition on using artificial intelligence to adjust product prices in real time based on market demands.
Prohibition on using competitor prices, inventory levels, or customer behavior to set prices.
Enforcement of this prohibition by the attorney general under section 8.31.

summary: Usage of artificial intelligence in the utilization review process prohibition provision

scope: This bill applies to utilization review organizations involved in health insurance processes. It targets entities that conduct reviews, evaluations, determinations, or appeals related to health insurance claims. The bill is relevant to both public and private healthcare providers engaged in utilization review.
modelsCovered: The bill covers the use of artificial intelligence as defined in United States Code, specifically targeting AI systems utilized in the utilization review process. It prohibits the use of any AI technologies in the review, evaluation, determination, or appeals processes of utilization review organizations.
keyRequirements: Prohibition on the use of artificial intelligence in the utilization review process.

summary: Health insurance; use of artificial intelligence prohibited in the utilization review process.

scope: This bill applies to utilization review organizations involved in health insurance processes. These organizations are responsible for evaluating and determining the necessity of healthcare services and treatments. The bill specifically targets entities engaged in the utilization review process within the healthcare sector.
modelsCovered: The bill covers the use of artificial intelligence as defined in United States Code, title 15, section 9401. It prohibits any form of artificial intelligence in the utilization review process, including evaluation, determination, or appeals related to healthcare services.
keyRequirements: Prohibition on the use of artificial intelligence in utilization review processes
Utilization review organizations are specifically prohibited from using AI in any part of their review, evaluation, determination, or appeals processes

summary: Cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence data centers sales exemption from certain energy savings goals provision

scope: This bill applies to cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence data centers that utilize electricity primarily for processing transactions involving digital currency. modelsCovered: The bill covers data mining facilities that process transactions involving digital currency, specifically cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence. It does not define specific AI models but implies the use of AI technologies in the context of cryptocurrency transactions.
keyRequirements: Exempt sales to cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence data centers from certain energy savings goals

summary: Individual communication with artificial intelligence disclosure requirement provision
title: A bill for an act relating to consumer protection; requiring persons to disclose that an individual is communicating with artificial intelligence
scope: This bill applies to individuals and businesses that engage in communication with consumers using artificial intelligence systems. It specifically targets entities that utilize AI in a manner that involves direct interaction with individuals, such as private companies and service providers that implement AI for customer communication.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems defined as machine-based systems that infer outputs from inputs to generate content, decisions, predictions, or recommendations. It includes AI systems that engage in textual or aural conversations with individuals, potentially misleading them into believing they are interacting with a human.
keyRequirements: Persons must disclose that an individual is communicating with artificial intelligence.

scope: This bill applies to government agencies and private entities involved in the development, deployment, or use of robotic devices that are classified as weapons. It targets organizations that manufacture or utilize such technologies, regardless of their size or revenue.
modelsCovered: The bill covers robotic devices that are classified as weapons, including those used for military or law enforcement purposes. It specifically addresses the deployment of autonomous systems that can operate without human intervention in combat or security scenarios.
keyRequirements: Establish safety protocols for the use of robotic devices in weaponry.
Ensure compliance with existing regulations on weaponry and robotics.
Conduct regular assessments of robotic systems to evaluate their operational safety.

title: Employment: artificial intelligence
scope: This bill applies to private companies and employers that utilize artificial intelligence technologies in their hiring processes and employment practices. It specifically targets organizations that implement automated decision-making systems affecting employee selection and management. The bill is relevant to entities operating within the state of California.
modelsCovered: The bill covers automated decision-making systems that are used in employment contexts, particularly those that may impact hiring decisions and employee evaluations. It includes high-risk AI systems that could lead to significant consequences for individuals based on their employment status or opportunities. Generative AI systems and other forms of AI that influence workplace dynamics are also addressed.
keyRequirements: Employers must disclose the use of AI in hiring processes.
Companies are required to conduct impact assessments of AI systems used in employment.
Employers must ensure transparency in AI decision-making processes.

summary: Concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
title: Concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
scope: This bill applies to developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems operating within the state of Colorado. It includes private companies and organizations that develop or utilize AI technologies for decision-making processes affecting consumers. Specific size thresholds include developers with annual revenues of less than $5,000,000 and deployers with fewer than 500 full-time equivalent employees.
modelsCovered: The bill covers high-risk artificial intelligence systems that make consequential decisions affecting consumers. This includes systems that may result in algorithmic discrimination or impact consumer rights in areas such as employment, education, and access to essential services. The definitions also encompass systems that utilize algorithms for decision-making in various sectors, including finance, healthcare, and housing.
keyRequirements: Developers must use reasonable care to protect consumers from known risks of algorithmic discrimination.
Deployers are required to conduct impact assessments to identify risks associated with high-risk AI systems.
Developers must disclose known risks of algorithmic discrimination to the attorney general and affected deployers.
Consumers must be informed when interacting with an AI system that it is an AI system.
Developers and deployers must maintain documentation regarding compliance for at least three years.

summary: Concerning public safety protection from the risks of artificial intelligence systems.
title: Concerning public safety protection from the risks of artificial intelligence systems.
scope: This bill applies to developers, defined as employers or entities that contract with five or more independent contractors in Colorado each year and have trained at least one foundation model at a significant computational cost. It includes both employees and independent contractors working on foundation models.
modelsCovered: The bill covers foundation artificial intelligence models, which are defined as AI models trained on broad data, using self-supervision in the training process, and applicable across a wide range of contexts. These models are significant in terms of their potential impact on public safety and security.
keyRequirements: Developers must not retaliate against workers for disclosing information about risks to public safety or security.
Developers are required to provide notice to all workers of their rights and responsibilities under the bill.
Developers must establish an internal process for anonymous disclosures regarding risks to public safety or security.
Developers must provide monthly updates to workers who make disclosures about the status of investigations.
Aggrieved workers may commence civil actions against developers for violations of the bill.

summary: Concerning the application of artificial intelligence to predict, prevent, or assist in fighting wildfires, and, in connection therewith, making an appropriation.
title: Concerning the application of artificial intelligence to predict, prevent, or assist in fighting wildfires, and, in connection therewith, making an appropriation.
scope: This bill applies to the division of fire prevention and control within the state government of Colorado. It mandates the appropriation of funds for the development of AI applications related to wildfire management. The bill also allows for contracting with third parties that have developed relevant AI tools.
modelsCovered: The bill covers applications of artificial intelligence that predict, mitigate, or assist in fighting wildfires. This includes AI systems that produce data for maps displaying vegetation classification, wildfire ignition potential, ongoing wildfire perimeters, and predictions of wildfire spread.
keyRequirements: The general assembly must appropriate $7,500,000 to the division of fire prevention and control for state fiscal year 2024-25.
The division is required to use the appropriated funds to study and develop AI applications for wildfire management.
The division may contract with third parties that have developed AI tools for wildfire prediction and mitigation.
The division is authorized to seek, accept, and expend gifts, grants, and donations for the purposes of the bill.

summary: To (1) establish various requirements concerning artificial intelligence systems, (2) require the Department of Economic and Community Development to (A) establish an artificial intelligence regulatory sandbox program, (B) plan to establish a technol...
title: AN ACT CONCERNING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
scope: This bill applies to developers, deployers, and integrators of high-risk artificial intelligence systems operating within the state. It encompasses private companies, government agencies, and individuals involved in the development or deployment of such systems. The bill mandates compliance from entities that utilize AI technologies that may impact consumers.
modelsCovered: The bill covers high-risk artificial intelligence systems that are intended to make consequential decisions affecting consumers. This includes systems that process personal data and may lead to algorithmic discrimination. Additionally, it addresses general-purpose artificial intelligence models capable of being used in high-risk applications.
keyRequirements: Developers must use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination risks.
Developers must provide documentation regarding the intended uses and known risks of high-risk AI systems.
Integrators must enter into contracts with developers to clarify responsibilities regarding high-risk AI systems.
Deployers must implement a risk management policy to govern the deployment of high-risk AI systems.
Deployers must complete impact assessments for high-risk AI systems at least annually.
Developers of general-purpose AI models must provide necessary documentation to assist deployers in compliance.
All entities must disclose to consumers when they are interacting with an AI system.

summary: To (1) limit the use of electronic monitoring by an employer, and (2) establish various requirements concerning the use of artificial intelligence systems by employers.
title: An Act Implementing Artificial Intelligence Protections for Employees
scope: This bill applies to employers, including any person, firm, or corporation, as well as the state and any political subdivisions that have employees. It specifically addresses the use of electronic monitoring and artificial intelligence systems in the workplace, impacting all employers regardless of size or industry sector.
modelsCovered: The bill covers high-risk artificial intelligence systems, which are defined as those that make or are a substantial factor in making consequential decisions affecting employees. It includes automated decision-making systems that may lead to algorithmic discrimination based on various protected characteristics.
keyRequirements: Employers must provide prior written notice to employees about the types of electronic monitoring that may occur.
Employers must conduct an impact assessment before deploying high-risk artificial intelligence systems.
Employers must implement human oversight over automated decision-making processes involving high-risk AI systems.
Employers cannot retaliate against employees for refusing to follow decisions made by high-risk AI systems if certain conditions are met.
Employers must disclose the purpose and nature of consequential decisions made by high-risk AI systems to affected employees.

summary: To criminalize unauthorized dissemination of intimate images that are digitally altered or created through the use of artificial intelligence.
title: AN ACT CONCERNING UNLAWFUL DISSEMINATION OF AN INTIMATE SYNTHETICALLY CREATED IMAGE
scope: This bill applies to individuals who intentionally disseminate intimate synthetically created images without the consent of the depicted person. It specifically targets those who disseminate such images through electronic or other means, and it includes provisions for harm caused to the depicted individuals.
modelsCovered: The bill addresses synthetically created images, which are defined as photographs, films, or other images that are not wholly recorded by a camera and are virtually indistinguishable from actual depictions of identifiable persons. This includes images generated partially or wholly by computer systems.
keyRequirements: Intentionally disseminate intimate synthetically created images without consent.
Ensure that the dissemination does not result in harm to the depicted individual.
Avoid liability for providers of interactive computer services for content provided by others.

summary: To require (1) an owner or operator of an artificial intelligence data center to submit quarterly reports to the Commissioner of Energy and Environmental Protection, and (2) the commissioner to adopt regulations concerning water and energy efficiency...
title: AN ACT REQUIRING A STUDY CONCERNING ENERGY EFFICIENCY REQUIREMENTS FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DATA CENTERS
scope: This bill applies to owners or operators of artificial intelligence data centers. It mandates compliance with reporting and regulatory requirements set forth by the Commissioner of Energy and Environmental Protection. The focus is on entities managing data centers that utilize significant energy resources.
modelsCovered: The bill addresses energy efficiency performance standards specifically for artificial intelligence data centers. It encompasses data centers utilizing renewable energy resources and those capable of participating in demand response programs.
keyRequirements: Owners or operators of artificial intelligence data centers must submit quarterly reports to the Commissioner of Energy and Environmental Protection.
The Commissioner must conduct a study on energy efficiency performance standards for artificial intelligence data centers.
The study must consider best practices for energy efficiency, energy management systems, renewable energy use, demand response program participation, and limitations on diesel backup generators.

title: AN ACT CONCERNING MINORS AND SOCIAL MEDIA
scope: This bill applies to social media platforms that target individuals younger than seventeen years of age. It specifically addresses the practices of these platforms in relation to minors, prohibiting certain targeted algorithms and content feeds.
modelsCovered: The bill covers social media algorithms that are designed to target minors. It specifically addresses algorithms that track personal information such as age or phone numbers to deliver targeted content.
keyRequirements: Prohibit any social media algorithm that targets individuals younger than seventeen years of age.
Prohibit tracking of individuals' age or telephone number for targeting purposes.
Prohibit inclusion of a continuous feed in the social media account of any individual younger than seventeen years of age.

summary: To prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to replace public school educators in providing instruction to and regular interaction with students.
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO REPLACE TEACHERS
scope: This bill applies to public school educators within the state of Connecticut. It specifically targets educational institutions that employ teachers to provide instruction and regular interaction with students.
modelsCovered: The bill covers the use of artificial intelligence systems that could potentially replace public school educators in their instructional roles. It addresses AI technologies that would be used in the context of education, particularly those that facilitate direct interaction with students.
keyRequirements: Prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to replace public school educators in providing instruction.
Ensure that public school educators maintain regular interaction with students without the involvement of AI.
Amend the general statutes to reflect these prohibitions.

modelsCovered: The bill covers the use of artificial intelligence systems that are employed as the primary method for denying health insurance claims. This includes automated decision-making systems that utilize AI technologies to evaluate and process claims.
keyRequirements: Prohibit any health insurer from using artificial intelligence as the primary method to deny health insurance claims.

summary: To establish a criminal offense for the creation and dissemination of artificial intelligence-generated pornography.
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE CREATION AND DISSEMINATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE -GENERATED PORNOGRAPHIC IMAGES OF A PERSON WITHOUT CONSENT
scope: This bill applies to individuals and entities involved in the creation and dissemination of artificial intelligence-generated pornographic images. It specifically targets those who create or distribute such content without the consent of the depicted individuals. This includes private companies and individuals engaged in the production or sharing of such materials.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence systems that are capable of generating pornographic images of individuals. This includes generative AI technologies that can create realistic images based on input data. The focus is on AI systems that produce content without the consent of the individuals represented in the generated images.
keyRequirements: Prohibit the creation of artificial intelligence-generated pornographic images without consent
Prohibit the dissemination of such images without consent

summary: To prohibit any health insurer from using a software tool, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence or an algorithm, to automatically downcode or deny a health insurance claim submitted by a health care provider without detailed review ...

scope: This bill applies to health insurers, specifically those involved in processing health insurance claims submitted by healthcare providers. It targets entities that utilize software tools for claim management, including private insurance companies operating within the state of Connecticut.
modelsCovered: The bill covers software tools used by health insurers, including artificial intelligence and algorithms, specifically in the context of automatically downcoding or denying health insurance claims. The focus is on automated decision-making systems that impact the processing of healthcare claims.
keyRequirements: Prohibit health insurers from using software tools to automatically downcode claims without detailed review.
Require detailed review of claims by a clinical peer before any downcoding or denial.
Amend title 38a of the general statutes to include these prohibitions.

The focus is on any AI technology that influences the approval or denial of health insurance claims.
keyRequirements: Prohibit any health insurer from using artificial intelligence to deny health insurance claims.

summary: To promote energy and water consumption efficiency in artificial intelligence data centers.

scope: This bill applies to artificial intelligence data centers that are required to meet specific energy and water efficiency standards. It targets private companies operating such data centers, focusing on those that utilize significant amounts of energy and water resources.
modelsCovered: The bill covers artificial intelligence data centers, which are facilities that house AI systems and technologies. It does not specify particular types of AI systems but emphasizes the operational requirements related to energy and water consumption.

Utilize energy storage systems and modern grid infrastructure
Implement water conservation measures

Safeguard patient access to procedures

modelsCovered: The bill addresses the use of artificial intelligence systems, particularly in the context of workforce automation. It seeks to study the fiscal impact and practicality of increasing artificial intelligence use by the state, which may include various AI technologies relevant to workforce management.

Assess the fiscal impact of increased artificial intelligence use by the state
Evaluate the automation of the size and scope of the state workforce
